body: My wife, our grandson Ryan and I parked our car at Ella railway station, on 23rd July 2019, and hired a tuk-tuk that took us first to the "Nine Arch Bridge" and then to Demodera railway station. We went there to see the famous 'spiral loop' at Demodera. The train coming from the up-country enters the tunnel located right under the station. Though at different levels, the tunnel is almost perpendicular to the station. It then traverses around the adjoining hill in an upward spiral coming up to the station and proceeds towards Ella. We observed the train passing along, after it emanated from the tunnel. When it arrived at the station we got in and travelled down to Ella. The legend has it that, during railway construction, engineers had been perplexed to find a means of bridging the considerable vertical level difference between two adjoining hills. A person tying his turban around his head is said to have implanted the idea of the loop to bridge this gap by circumscribing the hill. Demodera loop is 1049 feet feet long at a gradient of 1 in 44, the maximum allowable in Sri Lanka Railway construction. The quaint Demodera railway station reminded me of the time when I travelled to school by train. The trains in this section of the railway still rely on exchanging tablets on arrival. The ticket holding cupboard and even the appearance of the clock in the station master's room have remained unchanged from the 1950s. On the way back from Ella we passed over the 'Nine Arch Bridge', where there were many tourists waiting to see it pass by.
title: An Ingenious Solution !

body: The railway track coming out of a tunnel and going back above the same tunnel to reach the Demodara railway station, forms the loop. It was an interesting solution to an almost unique engineering challenge in the railway line by the British’s. It is certainly worth taking this train ride and when you get to go under the station you have just stopped at! Ride in 3rd class and watch the world go by while standing in the door! The cost is Rs 10 per person one way on the train from Ella to Demodera. This is just another amazing and marvelous piece of work. It is a great engineering marvel getting a train to rise-up in elevation on a mountain. You can go all the way to tunnel as well getting a nice experience. We caught the train to Demodara at 3:30pm from Ella. We got a fabulous 25 minute train trip over the bridge and through some tunnels; you see the loop at the Demodara station where the train goes around in a circle to descend 10 metres or so. Tuk tuk back to Ella was also a nice trip.Views from the train are stunning and well worth the effort. Local station will be able to advise of the scheduled train times and also if you download “Trains - Sri Lanka” App. If you get into a train coming from Badulla, it won’t be late but the one in opposite direction. It would be late as the trains commence from Colombo far away and mostly delays occur to giving way to the other train on opposite direction at stations as the railway line from Rabukkana onwards is single lined on the hills. What a view we got. The train came just 10 mins after we reach the station to take a glimpse and we saw road going upwards from the rail track. The train loops back and runs directly under the station! You can 'walk' the loop as well. If you want a bird's eye view you can go to Ooduwaare Estate where you can see the train loop round the hill and come back.For you to appreciate the loop better, get the tuk tuk driver and tell him to first take you down near the tunnel. And then you go back up to the Demodara railway station to watch the train leaving the tunnel from above.Can see a nice view from the Demodara train station. Once you get down from the train at Demodara station quickly run Out if the station to watch the train turn and come out of the tunnel going towards Badulla if you come on a Badulla bound train. The interesting thing behind this Demodara loop is taking a small train trip to cover the activity from Ella. It is a great thing to do with kids mainly and for adults too. It is definitely worth the sceneries even if you aren't a fan of trains! I recommend you take the train journey to cover the Demodera Loop.
title: Demodera Loop Is the Railway Track Going Back Above the Same Tunnel to Reach the Demodara Station is a Marvell.

body: Demodara loop, also known as the the spiral railway is recognised as one of the most fascinating civil engineering marvels in Sri Lanka. It is definitely one of the perfect spots for stunning pictures. The rail line passes under itself, going around the loop and emerging from a tunnel, which runs directly beneath the Demodara railway station. The rail loop is approximately 900 metres long and the tunnel is 320 metres in length. It is considered the only loop in the world with a railway station situated exactly over a tunnel at spiral loop

body: Demodara, on the Badulla Railway line, is the only place in Sri Lanka where the railway line does a complete loop, before exiting through a tunnel onto the Demodara railway bridge, when proceeding towards Badulla.If you prefer to travel along the loop, note that when proceeding towards Badulla, the loop is just AFTER the Demodara station.I prefer to walk the entire loop. Be sure to ascertain the train times beforehand, since you will need to walk through a tunnel.The railway is single-line, and this obviously means that when a train goes in one direction, another cannot come from the opposite direction for some time.Ideal for train-spotting.

body: Demodara loop was engineered to achieve the required climb/descend of the railway. The railway loops and goes under itself. You can view this from the Demodara Railway station (walk few meters from the platform). What you see is the railway going under where you're standing on. You actually can't see the whole loop together unless viewed from a helicopter. We did this excursion by boarding the Colombo to Badulla "Podi Menike" train at Diyatalawa Station at 3:30pm (as we were staying at Diyatalawa). You can board this train at Ella as well. If you're going directly to Demodara station to view this, please check train times to see at what times trains arrive/depart as this is not a line with a lot of trains. We got off at Demodara, and walked few meters where you can see the Railway underneath where it goes underneatch after the negotiating the loop. You see the same train that you arrived going underneath. After this, we walked down to the railway (easy walk downhill), and walked along to the bridge nearby. Then we walked along the Railway tunnel (this is the tunnerl under the Demodara station) and climbed up from the other side of the hill (somewhat steep but short climb). Tips:If you're coming here on board a Train, the Nine Arches Bridge is between Ella and Demodara Stations. Get on board a Badulla bound train at Ella (or prior to Ella) and you will be riding on the Nine Arches Bridge. Train ride is interesting specially for the kids. Take precaution but it's very interesting to ride by sitting on the steps at the doors. You see people from all walks of life on this train, and odd snack sellers selling delicious deviled prawns on the train. Several small vegetable gardens on the side of the railway, and several rail crossings. In the station you get onboard, be sure to check out the tablet exchange between the Train driver and the Station employee. This is the "permission" note for the train to proceed to the next station (as this is single line track).After viewing the Demodara loop, you can probably walk along the Railway back towards Ella and reach Nine Arches Bridge. We want to Nine Arches Bridge by Vehicles so I don't know how easy or difficult the walk along the railway is towards Nine Arches. See my review of Nine Arches Bridge separately. Tip: If planning to see both Demodara Loop and go to Nine Arches, I recommend following,- Use Badulla bound "Podi Menike" train to go to Demodara (reaches Demodara at around 4+pm). - See the Demodara Loop, and find your way to Nine Archers (either walk or via vehicles). - You can then see next Badulla bound train "Udarata Menike" at Nine Arches at around 5:30pm.
title: One of the few placed in the world to see Railway Loops!.

We opted to head over to the nearby bridge to catch the incoming train, since you can only see the train passing from one side and then reappearing around the mountain as it loops. The area around the bridge is rather scenic - although do note that there is a short hike and a few muddy steps to get there from the road.
title: Plan your visit to coincide with the train times

body: We got to Demodara by bus & tuktuk after visiting Halpewatta tea factory and bought tickets to Ella (10 rupees). We crossed the station car park to watch the train come out of the tunnel beneath our feet and start going up the loop, then went back to the platform to see the train arrive and get on for the journey to Ella. There was a busload of excited Sri Lankans at the station to watch, and yet more smiling locals on the train who made the journey fun by screaming in the two tunnels.

body: We went to ella railway station around 1pm on a saturday and wanted to do a train ride to see the views, etc. Ella railway is well maintained, all information on display, washrooms are OK. The info on display could be a bit confusing and we spoke with the station master he was so helpful. We were lucky that a train was suppose to arrive at 1.24, but was also late 30 minutes. From ella we took a ticket to demodara railway station, which was the next stop further into hill country. The ticket was just LKR 10 each.The ride was about 15minutes. Can see alot of greenery while travelling. If you are taking this ride you will go through two tunnels, one is the popular 9arch bridge tunnel as well and on top of the nine arch bridge. Its an experience. We got off the demodara station and then went to the viewing point to see the demodara loop. Same train goes under the station. Details about the loop are displayed at the station. After viewing the train going through the loop go read the details about the loop in the station. Workers at the station were so helpful as well. We took a threewheel ride from the station to ella town and was charged LKR 350 as the next train was at 6 in the evening. You also can walk from ella station via the tracks to demodara station passing the demodara nine arch bridge. The walk from ella to demodara station is 6kms, but only thing is no point if you do not see a train going through the loop to get the experience of viewing the demodara loop. So going in a train and getting off at the demodara loop will ensure you see what you want to see.Then from demodara station if you like you can walk to ella station again 6km instead if a tuk tuk ride. Demodara station to nine arch bridge 4kms. Nine arch to ella station, 2km. station to ella town maybe around 1km. Be carful the tracks can get very narrow some places.
title: Great train ride

body: The Demodara Loop is basically a Railway construction that circumnavigates a hillock in an attempt to negotiate a substantial elevation difference on the upcountry railway line in the village of Demodara. This is one of the two main attractions on this line - the other being the equally famous Nine Arch bridge located between the stations of Ella and Demodara some 2.5 kilometres away. What sets this apart from many other loops present on the upcountry line is perhaps the unique way it has been constructed; after passing Demodara station the track circles a hillock and proceeds to to travel past a tunnel that is bored right underneath the Demodara Station! If one times his/her visit properly, one can easily observe this phenomenon from the front compound of the station. If one happens to travel on the train from Badulla toward Colombo in the night mail train, he/she will be able to observe the bright light of the station a hundred feet above first from a distance and then arrive at the station minutes after which is quite magical.
title: A fine example of a Railway Loop construction on the upcountry Railway

body: Must see place if you are interested in Engineering. It was altitude difference they wanted to overcome in the prefixed regulations. There is a height limit allowed by Railway authorities when building a railway track. So to find a solution for the height difference they build a track looping under each other. So was terrains. To connect the lines they build two bridges using only Granite stones. It was an arch type bridges. One was 3-Arch and the other was 9-Arch. If you are passing Ella then please use Passara road about 01km and then use the left byroad to reach 9-Arch bridge. To visit 3-Arch bridge you should pass Demodara Railway station and travel about 2kms and on your left you will see the small wonder. All the credit and gratitude to the people who sacrifice their time to build this.
title: What a marvel of Railway engineering

title: An engineering masterpiece
body: The Demodara railway line winds its way and goes directly under the station through the tunnel inside a mountain.If you make your way to the back of the railway station (other side of where the tracks are), there is a look out point, where you can stand directly above the tunnel and see the train looping in order to arrive at the station. It is said that the idea of this loop suddenly occurred to the late Mr.D.J.Wimalasurendra who was the greatest Sri Lankan engineer, who masterminded the railway line, when he observed the Kangany who was supervising the workers, undo his 'talappa' (head gear) and re-tie it round his head in a circular motion! Walking along the railway lines in these area is not considered abnormal nor that you have a death wish, as trains come rarely and the laid back staff at the station would happily encourage you to do so giving the approximate time of the train's arrival! They may even show you the 150 year old equipment and explain its functions inside the Railway Master's Office!
